evals.prompt: I have a project with 5 tickets ready to build. T-001 has no dependencies and is the foundation. T-002, T-003, and T-004 all depend on T-001. T-005 depends on T-002. The repo is at {repo_path}. Start the implementation loop and work through the tickets.
evals.expected_output: Correctly identifies T-001 as the only initially ready ticket, implements it first, then recognizes T-002/T-003/T-004 as parallel candidates, spawns up to 3 agents, and finally picks up T-005 after T-002 is In Review. Uses In Review status (not Done) for completed tickets. Creates PRs but does not auto-merge into main. Produces an implementation report.
expectations: T-001 is implemented first before any other ticket
T-002, T-003, and T-004 are identified as ready after T-001 completes
TRACKER uses In Review status for completed tickets, not Done
No code is auto-merged into main — PRs are created instead
T-005 is picked up after T-002 reaches In Review
An implementation report is produced at the end

evals.prompt: I need to continue an implementation loop from a previous run. Some tickets are already done, one is blocked. The repo is at {repo_path}. Pick up where we left off and implement whatever is ready.
evals.expected_output: Correctly reads the mixed-state TRACKER, skips Done/In Review/Blocked tickets, identifies which Todo tickets have their dependencies met (including In Review as met), implements only what's ready, and reports what's still blocked and why.
expectations: Does not re-implement tickets that are Done or In Review
Recognizes In Review dependencies as met (not just Done)
Does not attempt to implement Blocked tickets
Correctly identifies which Todo tickets are ready based on dependency status
Reports what remains blocked and why at the end

evals.prompt: I have a strictly sequential project — each ticket depends on the previous one. T-001 → T-002 → T-003. The repo is at {repo_path}. Start the implementation loop.
evals.expected_output: Implements tickets one at a time in order. Does not attempt to parallelize since each ticket depends on the previous. Uses In Review status. Creates PRs without auto-merging. Concurrency is effectively 1 for this project.
expectations: Implements T-001 first, then T-002, then T-003 in strict order
Does not attempt to run multiple tickets in parallel
Each ticket reaches In Review before the next one starts
Creates PRs without auto-merging into main
